tasks.short: Add material to existing files or create new records.

steps.what: Collect filing packets from departmental mailboxes.
Search the catalogue for existing records and possible duplicates.
Resolve uncertain identities and decide whether a new record is necessary.
Attach material, enter metadata, and create records where required.
Place retained originals in labelled folders and record their locations.

tasks.design: Send filing packets directly into a controlled intake in the {DOCS}, removing mailbox collection. A deterministic integration matches stable identifiers, checks duplicates, and creates or updates records through configured forms; uncertain matches go to the file clerk. Location labels support the remaining physical filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departments supplied inconsistent identifiers, while attachments and record entries travelled separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing intake forms and record interfaces can be configured, with small matching integrations built faster using AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Duplicate identities, inherited permissions, and originals that must remain on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when similar names refer to different matters and preserving the provenance of an original.

ambition.what: Missing-document checks when a new project file opens.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time attaching files and more time resolving record identity problems. They can correct routine filing matches within delegated limits; access and retention decisions remain with record owners.

reach.task: Check whether a project handover contains its required records.
reach.learn: Project milestones, handover requirements, and document ownership.

evidence.claim: Self-service changes can flow into employee records and payroll; this supports the integration pattern, not a filing-specific result.
Stable identifiers, duplicate checks, and configured record forms can automate routine filing updates.

assumptions: The baseline is a hybrid office with digital records and some retained paper originals.
Filing packets already contain filing metadata; interpreting incoming text is covered in the reading task.
These occupational tasks overlap and their time shares must not be added into a job-level estimate.
Shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Consultation under national rules is included where the change affects staff duties or monitoring; elapsed consultation may exceed build time.
unknowns: The proportion of records requiring paper originals.
Availability of stable identifiers and supported write interfaces in the {DOCS}.
The clerk's authority to create records and correct matches.
Access lead times and consultation requirements under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Which required record operations are available through existing {DOCS} configuration?
new_work: Resolve unmatched identifiers and duplicate records.
Review failed imports and reconcile filing receipts.
Maintain field mappings and access tests.
tasks.statement: Add new material to file records or create new records as necessary.

tasks.short: Record borrowed physical files, follow up overdue loans and confirm their return.

steps.what: Record the file identifier, borrower and due date at physical handover.
Compare open loan entries with their due dates.
Send reminders to borrowers with overdue files.
Ask borrowers about missing files, disputed loans or requested extensions.
Check that the returned physical file matches the borrowed file.
Mark the loan as returned in the register.

tasks.design: Configure a loan register in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to file identifiers in the {DOCS}, with simple checkout and return forms. Due-date views and internal {EMAIL} reminders run from the register, while the clerk confirms physical handovers and handles custody disputes. Authorised staff can check availability without seeing protected file contents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper movement records did not generate reminders, and a separate loan application seemed disproportionate to the workload.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms, date rules and notifications can provide the register without model use or substantial custom development.
tasks.still_hard: An accurate register depends on staff recording actual handovers. Unlogged transfers, missing originals and disputed possession still require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Establishing who really holds an original and negotiating its return when operational needs conflict.

ambition.what: Self-service file availability checks for remote project teams.

tasks.altitude: Routine chasing falls away, leaving custody disputes and physical verification. Proposed delegation lets the clerk escalate overdue originals directly to record owners; access approval remains with those owners.

reach.task: Locate essential originals during a recovery exercise.
reach.learn: Recovery priorities, custody evidence and fallback storage arrangements.

evidence.claim: Loan registers, due-date calculations and reminders are deterministic configuration tasks.
Digital status cannot establish physical custody without a reliable handover or return confirmation.
Build ranges and remaining-time estimates describe a proposed pilot, not a documented case.

assumptions: Physical originals still need to circulate; replacing all loans with digital access is outside this pilot.
The baseline uses a paper loan register; some employers instead use the {DOCS} or a {SPREADSHEET}.
The human-task prior understates the removable due-date checking and reminder work in this baseline.
Borrowers are internal staff and reminders reveal only authorised file references.
The {WORKFLOW} can configure forms, date rules and role-based views.
GDPR applies to borrower records; consultation under national rules may apply to identifiable activity logging.
unknowns: Current register format and proportion of unlogged transfers.
Whether file identifiers and borrower directories are reliable.
Which files may be borrowed and who can grant extensions.
Whether the proposed availability service can expose safe metadata.
Applicable consultation requirements and access lead times.
research_questions: Can restricted digital copies remove some physical loans entirely?
Can existing labels support quick identifier capture?
Will borrowers consistently record onward transfers?
Which overdue cases need escalation rather than another reminder?
new_work: Correct missing or mistaken custody entries.
Handle bounced reminders and disputed loans.
Maintain due-date rules and borrower access.
Periodically compare a physical sample with the loan register.
tasks.statement: Track materials removed from files to ensure that borrowed files are returned.

tasks.short: Collect departmental records, check completeness and assemble materials for filing.

steps.what: Check filing schedules and departmental lists to identify materials due.
Request due materials from employees and department administrators.
Collect paper materials from departmental trays and employees.
Download emailed attachments and gather files from departmental folders.
Check required items, identifiers and versions before assembling the filing batch.
Resolve missing, disputed or unclear materials with the responsible employee.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to schedule collection requests and accept records through a structured intake linked to the {DOCS}. Deterministic connectors collect approved digital records and check required identifiers and items against filing checklists. The clerk reviews each assembled batch, collects remaining originals and resolves missing or disputed materials.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departments submitted records through different channels, and filing requirements were often informal.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, scheduled notifications and folder integrations already exist. AI-assisted coding can make the small connectors and validation rules cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Software cannot collect an original from a desk or establish that an unlisted record exists. Distinguishing a final version from a working draft can still require the record owner's explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk knows when a department has supplied the wrong material and can resolve the gap without creating unnecessary duplicate requests.

ambition.what: Filing-readiness checks before internal project closure.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time requesting and downloading records and more time resolving gaps. They can return incomplete batches against agreed checklists; record owners retain responsibility for substantive completeness.

reach.task: Check that project closure records are complete and assigned to an owner.
reach.learn: Closure milestones, document ownership and evidence checklists.

evidence.claim: Scheduled requests, structured submissions and required-field checks need deterministic workflow rather than an autonomous agent.
Rossum checks document-derived orders against rules and routes exceptions, supporting the validation-and-exception pattern.
The cited order-processing capability does not establish automated collection or completeness of departmental archives.

assumptions: Paper collection remains substantial, consistent with the supplied offline-work prior.
A department can define expected record types and required identifiers before automation.
Digital collection is limited to approved submission locations and permitted records.
Step shares and remaining time are estimates; the mix of originals and digital records determines savings.
Access and any consultation required under national rules are included in the build estimate.
unknowns: Which originals must be retained and which can use approved digital submissions.
Whether departmental record lists and final-version conventions are reliable.
Permissions and interfaces available for departmental folders and mail intake.
Who may accept an incomplete batch or change the filing checklist.
research_questions: Which completeness checks can be expressed as explicit rules?
Can direct submission eliminate attachment downloading without moving work onto employees?
Which submission events provide reliable final-version evidence?
new_work: Maintain filing checklists and submission ownership.
Review assembled batches and validation exceptions.
Handle connector failures and unexpected file formats.
Remove duplicate requests and adjust schedules when departments change.
tasks.statement: Gather materials to be filed from departments or employees.

tasks.short: Classify and order records using established filing guidelines.

steps.what: Retrieve the applicable filing rules for the batch.
Assign categories from dates, identifiers, document types, and other explicit filing metadata.
Resolve conflicting rules or missing filing information.
Apply catalogue labels and arrange the digital filing order.
Sort retained paper into the prescribed sequence.

tasks.design: Configure categories and catalogue ordering in the {DOCS}, adding a deterministic rule table only for rules it cannot express. Explicit metadata drives classification, while conflicting rules enter a review queue in the {WORKFLOW}. The same assignments generate labels for paper batches.
tasks.previous_blocker: Filing rules lived in guidance documents and personal knowledge rather than executable tables.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration and small rule translators can turn established guidelines into repeatable checks without requiring a model.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting departmental taxonomies, incomplete metadata, and physically sorting paper.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding why a classification matters to future users and spotting misleading category boundaries.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on recurring category conflicts.

tasks.altitude: The clerk reviews a shorter exception queue and brings concrete category conflicts to record owners. They gain delegated authority to resolve routine category ambiguities, while policy changes still require owner approval.

reach.task: Identify recurring handover failures from classification exceptions.
reach.learn: Process mapping, exception sampling, and distinguishing local mistakes from unclear rules.

evidence.claim: Alphabetical, chronological, numerical, and explicit metadata classification are deterministic operations.
Physical paper sorting remains manual unless document handling equipment or paper elimination changes the process.

assumptions: Reading free text to infer missing metadata is covered by the incoming-material task.
Classification labels do not automatically broaden access permissions.
Physical handling is represented as paper work, not assumed to be meetings.
Shares and build ranges are estimates for one shared filing taxonomy.
Applicable consultation under national rules is included in the access range.
unknowns: Whether filing rules are current, consistent, and approved.
How often classification depends on unstated local knowledge.
The volume of physical sorting.
Existing {DOCS} rule capabilities and access permissions.
research_questions: Can existing {DOCS} category and ordering features express the approved taxonomy without custom code?
new_work: Test rule changes against representative records.
Review conflicting categories and missing metadata.
Maintain category definitions and migration mappings.
tasks.statement: Sort or classify information according to guidelines, such as content, purpose, user criteria, or chronological, alphabetical, or numerical order.

tasks.short: Read incoming material to determine its filing destination.

steps.what: Open incoming material and check legibility, completeness, and attachments.
Read the content and identify its subject, record reference, and likely filing category.

loop.input: One readable document, approved category definitions, and permission-filtered record references.
loop.output: Suggested category and record reference, with supporting text spans or an abstention.
loop.check: Validate the output schema, allowed categories, cited spans, and record references; the clerk approves the suggestion.
loop.stop: One proposal and at most one schema repair per document; abstain on unresolved ambiguity or budget exhaustion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Some documents express their purpose indirectly and lack a reliable identifier; explicit identifiers bypass the model.

steps.what: Resolve unusual content or sensitivity concerns and record the final filing instructions.

tasks.design: Use configured text capture and quality checks in the {DOCS}, with exact identifiers handled by rules first. A bounded classifier proposes metadata for remaining free text and shows supporting passages beside the source. The clerk approves suggestions and resolves sensitive or ambiguous cases before filing instructions enter the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reading varied correspondence required context that filenames and fixed keyword rules did not reliably supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded models can propose structured labels from free text; schema checks and source passages make review practical.
tasks.still_hard: Poor scans, mixed subjects, unfamiliar terminology, and content whose sensitivity depends on organisational context.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a sensitive matter disguised as routine correspondence and asking the right record owner for context.

ambition.what: Guided filing intake for temporary project assistants.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time checking difficult documents and helping occasional filers. They can offer filing guidance within approved categories; they gain no authority to change access policy.

reach.task: Prepare complete project correspondence packets before handover.
reach.learn: Required attachments, subject references, and escalation routes for sensitive material.

evidence.claim: Rossum extracts information from order emails and documents and routes exceptions; this is adjacent capture evidence, not proof of general filing accuracy.
A bounded classifier can propose filing metadata, but accuracy and review time require testing on representative documents.

assumptions: Readable digital material is available; physically preparing damaged or bound originals remains manual.
Configured capture flags quality problems but cannot prove semantic completeness.
The final step handles exceptions and finalises instructions; routine proposal approval time is counted in the reading step.
Access controls also restrict model inputs and catalogue lookup.
This scope supports administrative filing, without employee evaluation or decisions about individual rights.
Shares and build ranges are estimates; applicable consultation under national rules is included.
unknowns: Document languages, scan quality, and the frequency of mixed-subject documents.
Whether approved processing arrangements permit confidential material in a model service.
Availability of labelled examples and clerk review capacity.
Who may decide sensitivity-related filing exceptions.
research_questions: How accurately does the classifier perform on each document class and language?
Does reviewing suggestions reduce total handling time while preserving filing quality?
Which GDPR and EU AI Act obligations apply to the selected processing arrangement and actual use?
new_work: Review proposals and resolve abstentions.
Sample approved classifications for errors.
Maintain category examples and capture settings.
Retest after model or document-template changes.
tasks.statement: Scan or read incoming materials to determine how and where they should be classified or filed.

tasks.short: Put classified physical records into the correct cabinets, boxes or shelves.

steps.what: Look up the storage location for each identified record.
Carry and place the material in its assigned receptacle.
Record the final box or shelf location in the storage register.

tasks.design: Configure a storage register in the {DOCS} with record identifiers, box identifiers and permitted locations. A mobile form in the {WORKFLOW} shows the destination and checks scanned record and location codes; the clerk moves the material and confirms placement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical movement cannot be replaced by a records application. Manual location lookup and later register updates added avoidable handling time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and barcode input can connect placement to the register. Small configuration changes and adapters are cheaper to build, but moving paper remains physical work.
tasks.still_hard: Full shelves, damaged boxes, restricted storage and oversized materials need local handling. A matching scan does not prove that the material was placed correctly.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unsafe storage, damaged materials and practical placement problems that the location register cannot see.
tasks.altitude: Most of the clerk’s week remains physical filing. Lookup and register entry shrink, but decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan archive space and resolve unsuitable storage conditions.
reach.learn: Learn capacity measurement, safe handling and how to report storage-condition problems.

evidence.claim: Identifier-to-location lookup and scan validation are deterministic records-app functions.
This design reduces lookup and recording effort while retaining physical placement.

assumptions: This task concerns physical records that the company has decided to retain.
The storage register can represent cabinets, boxes and shelf positions.
Time shares are estimates consistent with the strong physical-work prior.
Mobile access or a nearby terminal is practical in the storage area.
GDPR applies to personal records and location metadata. National rules determine any consultation needed for scan logs; no employee scoring is proposed.
Build ranges cover one storage area and existing mobile equipment.
unknowns: Are storage locations consistently labelled and recorded?
Can existing equipment read record and location codes?
How often do clerks encounter full or unsuitable locations?
Which paper copies could be avoided under the company’s approved retention arrangements?
research_questions: How much time is spent walking, looking up locations and entering confirmations?
Would ordered filing batches reduce walking without delaying urgent records?
Can the form prevent incorrect location entries without adding more handling?
new_work: Replace unreadable location labels.
Resolve scan mismatches and unavailable destinations.
Maintain the storage register when boxes or shelves move.
Sample physical placements against recorded locations.
tasks.statement: Place materials into storage receptacles, such as file cabinets, boxes, bins, or drawers, according to classification and identification information.

tasks.short: Classify incoming records, assign identifiers and mark materials for filing.

steps.what: Read incoming materials for record type, date and reference details.

loop.input: A digital record or scanned pages and the required metadata schema.
loop.output: Record details with supporting page references and unreadable fields flagged.
loop.check: Validate field formats and references; the clerk checks uncertain or conflicting values.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry; unreadable or incomplete records enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured source records bypass extraction; varied legacy pages lack consistent field positions and wording.

steps.what: Select the classification code from the filing scheme.
Assign an identification number and enter the index record.
Stamp or label the physical material with its identifier.

tasks.design: Configure classification choices, unique identifiers and required fields in the {DOCS}, importing metadata directly from connected source records. A bounded extraction loop prepares metadata for irregular documents; the clerk confirms classification, and an artefact generator produces labels for retained paper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metadata was retyped from paper and separate sources. Local classification habits and identifier collisions discouraged unattended indexing.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured fields, unique-number sequences and imports handle most indexing. Bounded extraction helps with variable documents, and AI-assisted coding makes small adapters cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous record types, poor scans and unidentified attachments need a person. Physical labels must still be attached to the correct material.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve records that span several categories and recognise when a classification would hide an important relationship.

ambition.what: Provide a missing-metadata return queue for departments submitting incomplete records.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time copying identifiers and more time resolving incomplete submissions. They can request corrections through the queue; changes to the filing scheme still need approval.

reach.task: Validate incoming batch records before import.
reach.learn: Learn schema validation, duplicate detection and how to trace errors to source submissions.

evidence.claim: Configurable identifier sequences, required metadata and classification lists can handle structured indexing without a model.
Rossum documents extraction, validation and exception routing for orders; this supports an adjacent capture pattern, not file-classification accuracy.
Attaching labels to retained paper remains physical work in the proposed design.

assumptions: The company has an approved filing scheme and retains some physical records.
Common classification codes can be suggested using explicit metadata mappings.
Time shares are estimates; the high offline prior is interpreted as paper handling, not meeting time.
Digital records arriving with complete source metadata bypass the extraction loop.
GDPR applies where metadata identifies people; EU AI Act applicability depends on use. National rules determine consultation requirements.
Build ranges cover one record family, repository and label format, with shared capture infrastructure where available.
unknowns: Does the repository support numbering, classification lists and metadata imports?
What proportion of records arrives with usable structured metadata?
Are existing identifiers unique across departments?
Must originals be stamped, labelled or left unmarked?
research_questions: Which fields can be imported directly instead of extracted?
How often do explicit mappings produce a single valid classification?
Can duplicate submissions be detected without confusing distinct versions?
new_work: Review uncertain metadata and classification suggestions.
Resolve duplicate identifiers and resubmitted records.
Maintain source-field mappings and extraction samples.
Check label readability and label-to-record matching.
tasks.statement: Assign and record or stamp identification numbers or codes to index materials for filing.

tasks.short: Answer coworkers’ questions about record contents, status and location.

steps.what: Clarify which record and information the requester needs.
Check requester access against record restrictions.
Search the index for matching records and current locations.
Read matching records and assemble the requested information.

loop.input: The clarified question and authorised record passages with stable references.
loop.output: An answer draft with passage references and explicit information gaps.
loop.check: Validate references and access again; the clerk checks meaning before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; missing or conflicting evidence goes to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Location and status use fixed fields; questions about document meaning require reading varied prose.

steps.what: Send the answer or explain why further clarification is needed.

tasks.design: Configure a request form and permission-filtered search in the {WORKFLOW} and {DOCS}. Fixed fields answer location and status questions; a bounded reading loop drafts content answers with source passages, and the file clerk approves release through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent indexing and access rules made search unreliable. Questions arrived without enough identifiers, and answers required opening several documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, identity controls and forms cover the structured work. AI-assisted coding reduces connector effort, while bounded reading can prepare answers from authorised passages.
tasks.still_hard: Missing records, conflicting versions and requests involving another person’s confidential information still need investigation. Paper-only records require physical retrieval.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently simple question needs context, discretion or a conversation with the record owner.

ambition.what: Give remote project coordinators access to permission-filtered record location and status lookup.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time finding routine answers and more time resolving missing or contradictory records. Access exceptions remain with the record owner; no new disclosure rights are assumed.

reach.task: Prepare document packs for recurring meetings.
reach.learn: Learn version selection, meeting context and how to assemble a complete authorised pack.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk Robin answers from a knowledge base and creates a pre-filled request when it cannot answer.
Permission-filtered record search and cited answer drafting are a proposed application, not a documented file-clerk case.
GDPR Article 22 concerns solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; record lookup alone is not such a decision.

assumptions: Requests mainly come from coworkers, and most frequently requested records have digital copies.
Today's means and time shares are planning estimates, not measured observations.
Structured lookup is more prominent than the supplied means prior suggests; informal questioning still occurs by phone.
Access rules are approved independently; the solution cannot grant access.
GDPR applies to personal records. EU AI Act duties depend on the deployed function; national rules determine employee consultation requirements.
Build ranges cover one repository and one request channel; consultation and access lead time may overlap other work.
unknowns: Which records are digital, searchable and correctly permissioned?
How often do questions require paper retrieval or external disclosure?
Who approves access exceptions and disputed record interpretations?
What consultation and access approvals are required locally?
research_questions: On a representative question sample, how many answers come entirely from index fields?
Does search exclude restricted titles, snippets and cached answers?
How reliably can reviewers detect unsupported statements in draft answers?
new_work: Review content answers before release.
Handle missing records, uncertain identities and access exceptions.
Maintain index synonyms, access mappings and answer evaluation samples.
Remove stale cached answers when records or permissions change.
tasks.statement: Answer questions about records or files.

tasks.short: Improve filing structures, agree changes and implement a tested migration.

steps.what: Review filing errors, retrieval delays and the current structure.
Discuss retrieval needs and filing problems with record users.
Draft a revised filing scheme and old-to-new mapping.

loop.input: User requirements, current categories, issue examples and approved access and retention constraints.
loop.output: A proposed scheme, migration mapping and unresolved design questions.
loop.check: Check category coverage, unique identifiers and preserved constraints; the clerk reviews meaning and usability.
loop.stop: One proposal and one revision; unresolved categories remain for a human design session.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can format the proposal, but reconciling conflicting descriptions and category meanings requires interpretation.

steps.what: Approve the revised scheme, permissions and migration scope.
Configure the approved structure in a test environment.
Test representative retrievals and approve readiness for migration.
Migrate approved records and reconcile the final index.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produces filing-quality measures from the {DOCS}, and a bounded drafting loop prepares scheme proposals for discussion. After the records owner approves the change, versioned scripts configure and test the structure; an accepted test result releases a logged migration with count, identifier and permission reconciliation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Filing changes required manual inventories, mappings and repeated configuration. Hidden dependencies and weak rollback plans made even modest improvements expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can accelerate reports, migration scripts and validation tooling. Existing export and configuration interfaces still determine what can be automated.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing categories that work across departments requires negotiation and retrieval testing. Legacy permissions, retention obligations and broken references can make migration costly.
tasks.human_edge: Understand how people look for records and settle category choices when departments use the same words differently.

ambition.what: Run a quarterly filing-improvement review using failed retrievals and misclassification evidence.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less project time compiling inventories and configuring repetitive changes, and more time testing retrieval with users. They can prioritise improvement proposals; approval of permissions, retention and migration scope remains with the records owner.

reach.task: Evaluate document retrieval processes across departments.
reach.learn: Learn process sampling, baseline measurement and how to distinguish taxonomy problems from training problems.

reach.task: Specify record migration and access-control requirements.
reach.learn: Learn identifier mapping, dependency tracing, acceptance criteria and rollback design.

evidence.claim: Inventory reports, mapping validation and repeatable migrations can use deterministic code; category design still needs human judgement.
Bounded drafting can prepare a filing proposal, but the digest provides no documented filing-system redesign case.

assumptions: A records owner can approve the scheme and an administrator controls repository configuration.
The repository supports exports, a test area and reversible configuration or migration operations.
Migration preserves originals and does not delete records or change retention without separate approval.
Time shares are estimates for a modest redesign; meetings are concentrated in requirements and approval.
GDPR applies to personal records. EU AI Act applicability depends on the actual function; national rules determine employee consultation requirements.
Build ranges cover one repository and a limited set of record classes, excluding large-scale paper reboxing.
unknowns: How many record classes, repositories and external links are affected?
Are retention and permission rules documented and consistent?
Who has authority to approve the scheme and accept migration tests?
Can the repository preserve identifiers, links and access rights during migration?
What national consultation requirements and internal change procedures apply?
research_questions: Which retrieval failures arise from category design rather than missing metadata?
Can a proposed scheme improve representative retrievals without increasing filing errors?
Can migration checks detect changed permissions, missing records and broken references?
Does a pilot demonstrate a complete rollback before wider migration?
new_work: Maintain retrieval test cases and filing-quality measures.
Review proposed categories with record users.
Maintain migration scripts and configuration versions.
Investigate reconciliation failures and stop affected migration batches.
Update filing guidance and support users after rollout.
tasks.statement: Modify or improve filing systems or implement new filing systems.

tasks.short: Inspect physical and digital files for correct placement, readability and condition, then record defects.

steps.what: Select files for inspection and prepare the location checklist.
Compare physical file labels and shelf positions with the checklist.
Inspect physical pages and folders for legibility, damage and deterioration.
Open digital files and check their placement and readability.
Copy inspection findings into the central defect log.
Approve relocation, rescanning or conservation work for defective files.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} prepares inspection checklists from the {DOCS} and captures physical findings directly into a defect register, removing separate transcription into the {SPREADSHEET}. Deterministic checks on the {DATA_PLATFORM} flag unreadable digital containers, missing files and placement mismatches, with human review for meaningful readability. Physical inspection remains with the clerk, and record owners approve corrective work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical condition could not be inferred from the index, while separate checklists and defect logs made even simple inspection support cumbersome.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured inspection forms and small file-validation routines can reduce preparation and paperwork. They require no breakthrough in interpreting physical damage.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile originals, faint annotations and deterioration require direct inspection and sometimes specialist conservation advice. A technically readable digital file may still be incomplete or unusable.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a record remains usable and recognising damage that threatens evidential value.

ambition.what: Weekly reprioritisation of inspections for fragile originals.

tasks.altitude: Physical inspection still occupies most of the work; preparation and transcription shrink. Proposed delegation lets the clerk reorder inspections within an approved risk policy, while corrective expenditure remains with record owners.

reach.task: Develop a defensible sampling plan for record inspections.
reach.learn: Defect classification, sample bias and evidence needed to close corrective actions.

evidence.claim: File existence, container readability and metadata placement can be checked deterministically.
Technical checks cannot establish physical condition or complete semantic readability.
Configured inspection forms can remove separate transcription; proposed savings and build ranges remain estimates.

assumptions: The workload includes physical originals and a smaller digital inspection branch.
The baseline uses a {SPREADSHEET} to consolidate findings, exceeding that means prior.
Physical inspection volume is unchanged; savings come from preparation, supported placement checks and logging.
Findings are captured during inspection, allowing the later copying step to disappear.
The {WORKFLOW} supports inspection forms and restricted defect records.
GDPR applies where inspected records contain personal data; consultation under national rules may apply to identifiable activity logging.
unknowns: Physical-to-digital file mix and required inspection coverage.
Existing defect log, file labels and location accuracy.
Which records require specialist conservation or stricter handling.
Who may approve relocation, rescanning and conservation spending.
Applicable consultation requirements and permissions for digital validation.
research_questions: Which digital defects can be detected without exposing document content?
Can existing labels speed placement checks without new equipment?
Which findings require full inspection rather than sampling?
Can direct capture preserve enough evidence to remove the separate defect log?
new_work: Review digital check failures and false alarms.
Maintain inspection criteria and defect categories.
Check that direct capture remains complete.
Track approved corrective work to closure.
Revisit inspection priorities when new defect patterns appear.
tasks.statement: Perform periodic inspections of materials or files to ensure correct placement, legibility, or proper condition.

tasks.short: Archive or destroy records according to retention rules and approved disposal decisions.

steps.what: Find records due for retention review and assemble a candidate list.
Check candidates against legal holds, open matters, and retention exceptions.
Approve archival transfers or destruction, and defer unresolved cases.
Move approved digital records into inactive storage.
Box approved paper records and record their inactive storage locations.
Delete approved digital records and capture the disposal log.
Release approved paper batches for secure destruction.
Reconcile storage receipts and destruction certificates with the approved batch.

tasks.design: Configure retention candidates, archival moves, and disposal logs in the {DOCS}, with recorded action approvals in the {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic check joins candidates to the hold register and rechecks holds before execution; missing retention rules or unresolved holds block disposal. The clerk handles paper custody and reconciles evidence, while record owners approve the specific records and actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Retention dates, hold notices, physical locations, and approvals were maintained separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing retention features and small integrations can assemble reviewable batches and enforce recorded approvals.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting retention exceptions, discovering undocumented holds, deleting across replicas, and maintaining physical chain of custody.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when an apparently expired record still supports an open dispute or obligation and escalating before destruction.

ambition.what: Weekly triage of blocked retention cases.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching for due records and more time resolving holds and verifying custody evidence. They can prioritise exception investigations; destruction authority stays with record owners.

reach.task: Check that inactive records remain retrievable during disruption.
reach.learn: Recovery requirements, archive retrieval tests, and the relationship between backups and retention.

evidence.claim: Retention dates, hold matching, approval checks, and disposal logging can use deterministic workflows.
GDPR storage limitation must be reconciled with applicable retention obligations and holds; national rules vary.
Physical destruction and uncertain retention exceptions still require human handling and accountability.

assumptions: The scope covers routine business records with an approved retention schedule.
Archival transfer and destruction are alternative paths for individual records; shares describe aggregate batch work.

tasks.statement: Eliminate outdated or unnecessary materials, destroying them or transferring them to inactive storage, according to file maintenance guidelines or legal requirements.

tasks.short: Operate rotating archive equipment to bring physical files within reach.

steps.what: Look up the requested file's tray location in the {DOCS} catalogue.
Select the tray and operate the {OTHER} mechanized archive controller.
Remove the labelled file from the positioned tray.
Check the file identity and requester access before releasing the file.
Enter the borrower and file location in the {DOCS} checkout register.

tasks.design: Configure the {DOCS} catalogue and checkout register so a retrieval request supplies the tray location and prefills the borrower record. The file clerk operates the {OTHER} mechanized archive controller, verifies the physical file and confirms its checkout.
tasks.previous_blocker: The request, location catalogue and checkout register are separate. Older equipment may offer only local controls.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked records and form defaults can remove repeated lookup and typing. Small imports or extensions are easier to build with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Physical extraction, equipment faults and misfiled folders remain. Controller integration may cost more than the clerical time it saves.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize misfiled records and operate physical equipment safely.
tasks.altitude: The file clerk does less lookup and register entry while physical handling remains central. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan maintenance for mechanized archive equipment.
reach.learn: Fault categories, service intervals and how to report recurring equipment problems.

evidence.claim: Linked catalogue and checkout records can reduce repeated entry without automating physical equipment operation.
Build ranges and remaining time are planning estimates. They exclude controller modification and equipment replacement.

assumptions: The company retains mechanized physical filing equipment.
A digital catalogue and checkout register exist but are used separately.
Local equipment controls and existing safety interlocks remain in use.
Access design follows GDPR. National rules determine consultation requirements if checkout logging changes employee monitoring.

Resolve checkout discrepancies and overdue returns.
Review access permissions for borrower records.

tasks.statement: Operate mechanized files that rotate to bring needed records to a particular location.

tasks.short: Design filing forms that capture the information needed to classify, locate and control records.

steps.what: Discuss filing needs and recurring errors with the requesting team.
Define fields, identifiers and access requirements in a document.
Lay out a draft filing form using a document template.
Test the draft against sample records and record needed corrections.
Approve the tested form's fields, access and filing instructions.
Publish the approved form in the {DOCS} and retire its previous version.

tasks.design: Configure reusable filing forms in the {WORKFLOW}, with standard fields, identifier checks and approved access settings; link them from the {DOCS}. Native validation checks routine inputs, the file clerk tests usability, and publication runs only after the administrative services manager approves the specific version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms were separate documents, so layout, validation and version replacement required repeated manual work. Different teams used inconsistent field names.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing form builders supply reusable fields, validation and approval flows. AI-assisted coding can shorten small extensions where configuration falls short.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing necessary fields and understandable filing instructions needs operational knowledge. Unusual record types and paper-only users require extra testing.
tasks.human_edge: Find the minimum information people can reliably supply and resolve competing filing needs.

ambition.what: Rapid filing-form pilot for a new departmental record type.

tasks.altitude: The file clerk spends less time on layout and version replacement, leaving more time to test forms with users. With delegated authority, they can choose pilot fields and validation rules; final publication approval stays with the administrative services manager.

reach.task: Identify why records arrive incomplete or cannot be found.
reach.learn: Process mapping, error sampling and measuring first-submission completeness.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports self-service changes flowing into payroll, demonstrating an adjacent form-to-record pattern.
Reusable field definitions, native validation and version-specific approval can support filing-form design without a model loop.
Build ranges and time reductions are planning estimates for a small initial form set.

assumptions: A configurable {WORKFLOW} is available with forms, validation and version-specific approvals.
The initial scope covers one departmental form family.
A reusable field library supports the estimated reduction in field-definition time.
The administrative services manager is the designated publication approver.
GDPR governs personal data fields and access. Applicable EU AI Act duties are assessed if AI features are introduced; national rules govern employee consultation.

Required record identifiers, retention rules and sensitive fields.
Paper-form and accessibility requirements.

Applicable national consultation requirements.

Review accessibility and access settings before publication.
Handle submissions rejected by new validation.
Measure form errors and revise confusing instructions.
Maintain version links and any small extensions.
tasks.statement: Design forms related to filing systems.

tasks.short: Find archived microfilm or microfiche and load the requested record into a viewer.

steps.what: Match the retrieval request to a reel or fiche in the paper catalogue.
Collect the reel or fiche from archive storage.
Load the {OTHER} microfilm viewer and advance to the requested frame.
Confirm the frame and requester access before handing over the viewer.

tasks.design: Configure a searchable archive catalogue in the {DOCS}, linking record identifiers to storage locations and access rules. A request form in the {WORKFLOW} returns the location; the file clerk retrieves the carrier, operates the {OTHER} microfilm viewer and checks access before disclosure.
tasks.previous_blocker: The catalogue may be on paper, while retrieval requires physical handling. Digital lookup cannot load or navigate an old viewer.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records features can provide searchable locations and request forms. AI-assisted coding can shorten any small catalogue import work; no model is needed for exact lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Poor catalogue entries, damaged film and missing frame references remain costly. Bulk scanning is a separate project.
tasks.human_edge: Handle fragile carriers and distinguish the correct record when labels or frames are unclear.
tasks.altitude: The file clerk spends less time searching the catalogue but still handles carriers and viewers. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare complete archive retrieval requests.
reach.learn: Record identifiers, access rules and the difference between a catalogue entry and the original record.

evidence.claim: A structured catalogue supports deterministic location lookup; carrier handling and viewer operation remain physical.
Build ranges and time shares are planning estimates, not measured results. They exclude bulk scanning.

assumptions: This supplementary task describes a company retaining a legacy film archive, not every mid-size company.
The initial scope covers one bounded catalogue with stable record identifiers.
The time estimates retain all physical retrieval work.
Access design follows GDPR. Deployment checks applicable EU AI Act duties and national rules on employee consultation.
unknowns: Catalogue size, format and accuracy.
Viewer condition and available frame references.
Record sensitivity and requester access rules.
Available {DOCS} catalogue features and access permissions.
Applicable national consultation requirements.

Correct location entries when carriers move.

Maintain catalogue access permissions.
tasks.statement: Retrieve documents stored in microfilm or microfiche and place them in viewers for reading.

tasks.short: Enter and update file identifiers and document metadata so records can be retrieved.

steps.what: Open incoming records and locate their source identifiers.
Read the record and select its file number and document codes.

loop.input: Source record, allowed document codes and file register.
loop.output: Proposed metadata with source locations and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate schema, allowed codes, identifier existence and source evidence; clerk approves the draft.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation retry per record; unresolved fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Map structured fields directly; a bounded extraction loop handles metadata buried in free text.

steps.what: Enter or amend metadata in the document register.
Test retrieval and correct rejected or conflicting entries.

tasks.design: An intake integration maps structured metadata directly into the {DOCS} index draft and uses bounded extraction for free-text fields. The clerk approves the draft, then configured forms save it and deterministic checks test identifiers, duplicates and retrieval. A small exception queue in the {WORKFLOW} holds conflicting entries with their source evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source identifiers and filing codes were inconsistent, and connecting intake to the index required bespoke work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing metadata features, reusable connectors and faster implementation of mapping and validation code reduce setup effort. Bounded extraction can handle the minority of unstructured inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous ownership, duplicate identifiers and inherited filing conventions require local knowledge. Access filters must apply before extraction and retrieval.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when two similar records represent different matters and resolving ambiguous filing intent.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on recurring indexing errors and their source corrections.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving index exceptions and improving source quality. Proposed delegation lets the clerk correct approved metadata mappings; record access and retention decisions stay with record owners.

reach.task: Find recurring identifier errors across intake sources.
reach.learn: Field validation, master-data matching and safe correction procedures.

evidence.claim: Structured metadata mapping, code validation and retrieval checks can use deterministic rules.
Rossum documents extraction from email and PDF, rule checks and exception routing for orders; this is adjacent evidence.
The proposed time reductions and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured filing outcomes.

tasks.statement: Input data, such as file numbers, new or updated information, or document information codes into computer systems to support document and information retrieval.

tasks.short: Handle routine correspondence, calls, document preparation, office equipment and confidential materials.

steps.what: Open, sort and route incoming correspondence.
Answer calls, establish the caller's need and handle sensitive conversations.
Record call messages and forward them to the responsible colleague.
Type, format and check routine documents from instructions and templates.

loop.input: Document instructions, approved template and supplied facts.
loop.output: Draft document with unsupported or missing facts marked.
loop.check: Validate required fields and supplied facts; the file clerk checks wording before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; incomplete or failed checks return to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill fixed fields, but varied prose instructions sometimes require a bounded drafting step.

steps.what: Scan, copy or print materials and check page completeness.
Place confidential originals in restricted storage and secure work areas.

tasks.design: Configure intake queues, routing rules and short message forms in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to the {DOCS}. Generate routine documents from approved templates, using a bounded drafting loop only for prose instructions and clerk approval before release. Digital delivery reduces printing; physical handling and sensitive calls remain with the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixed paper and digital work, inconsistent templates and fragmented routing made small improvements costly to assemble.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, templates and routing features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting them; drafting models can handle a narrow prose step.
tasks.still_hard: Opening envelopes, handling originals and securing rooms remain physical work. Confidential content needs appropriate GDPR controls; any recording or employee monitoring requires separate assessment under EU law and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk recognises distress, ambiguous requests and situations where a confidential document should not enter the routine queue.

ambition.what: Template-based document preparation for shift supervisors.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer formatting jobs and message transfers. The clerk can resolve routine routing exceptions within an agreed directory, while records owners retain disclosure authority.

reach.task: Prepare routine correspondence from approved templates.
reach.learn: Template field design, plain-language checking and document version control.

evidence.claim: Forms, templates and routing rules can reduce routine office administration; physical handling remains.
TOPdesk Robin can answer from a knowledge base or create a pre-filled request, supporting the intake pattern.
Bounded drafting from supplied facts is feasible, but the digest provides no measured file-clerk case.

Maintain templates and routing contacts.
Handle failed scans and misrouted items.
Periodically verify access settings on generated documents.
tasks.statement: Perform general office activities, such as typing, answering telephones, operating office machines, processing mail, or securing confidential materials.

tasks.short: Track filed and withdrawn materials, reconcile movements and produce inventory reports.

steps.what: Record item identifiers, locations and borrowers on movement slips.
Transcribe movement slips into the electronic file register.
Compare register exports with slips and track overdue or unmatched movements.
Contact borrowers, investigate discrepancies and confirm corrections.
Generate and circulate filing, withdrawal and overdue-item reports.

tasks.design: Configure a movement register in the {DOCS}, capturing item and borrower identifiers at handover so paper slips and transcription disappear. A deterministic reconciliation job flags overdue items and conflicting movements, while scheduled reports show inventory and recovery actions. The clerk investigates disputed movements and confirms corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handovers were separate from the electronic register, and identifiers were not consistently captured at source.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records features and identifier scanning may cover the register. Small deterministic connectors and reports are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding; no model is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded handovers, missing labels and disputed custody cannot be solved from register data alone. Borrower logs need proportionate access and retention under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk establishes what actually happened when the physical item and the register disagree.

ambition.what: Weekly recovery priorities for overdue originals.

tasks.altitude: Routine logging and report preparation shrink substantially. The clerk gains discretion to prioritise recovery follow-up within agreed deadlines; write-offs and retention decisions remain with records owners.

reach.task: Prioritise document-recovery work and identify recurring custody failures.
reach.learn: Exception ageing, custody controls and service reporting.

evidence.claim: Identifier capture, movement validation and scheduled inventory reports are deterministic records functions.
AFAS self-service changes flow into payroll, illustrating capture once and reuse across systems, rather than physical-file tracking.
The digest contains no documented file-register case supporting a specific saving.

Direct capture replaces duplicate transcription, but scanning or selecting identifiers still takes human time.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates.

Investigate unmatched or conflicting events.
Monitor failed captures and reconciliation jobs.
Review report access and remove obsolete borrower data under approved retention rules.
tasks.statement: Keep records of materials filed or removed, using logbooks or computers and generate computerized reports.

tasks.short: Find requested records, retrieve originals or copies and deliver them to authorized users.

steps.what: Receive and record the request, requester and required delivery date.
Interpret vague descriptions and clarify which records the requester needs.

loop.input: Request text and permitted filing taxonomy.
loop.output: Proposed identifiers, dates, record types and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate fields against the taxonomy; the clerk confirms the interpretation before use.
loop.stop: One extraction and one clarification cycle; unresolved ambiguity returns to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured requests need no model, but informal descriptions can refer indirectly to record types or dates.

steps.what: Search indexes and folders to identify matching records and storage locations.
Retrieve requested paper originals from cabinets or archive storage.
Check requester authority and approve restricted or exceptional disclosure.
Prepare approved copies, checking pages, versions and required exclusions.
Deliver approved records to the authorized requester and record the handover.

tasks.design: Configure request intake and permission-filtered search in the {DOCS}, with the {WORKFLOW} managing exceptional access approvals and delivery logs. A bounded loop proposes search fields for vague requests; configured search and deterministic copy assembly handle the remaining digital work. Approved internal deliveries use controlled links, while the clerk handles originals and checks copy exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent indexing, paper archives and email requests required a clerk to bridge search, permission checks and delivery.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, access controls and workflow features cover routine retrieval. Small integrations are cheaper to assemble, and a bounded extraction loop can translate informal requests into search fields.
tasks.still_hard: Poor indexing and missing originals limit retrieval regardless of the model. Context-dependent disclosure and redaction require people; permission filtering must protect search results, previews and delivery under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk distinguishes a plausible match from the correct record and notices when a request could disclose more than intended.

ambition.what: Permission-checked evidence packs for internal project reviews.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching and forwarding routine files and more time resolving uncertain matches and disclosure exceptions. They can curate evidence packs within existing access rights; records owners retain authority to expand access.

reach.task: Assemble source-linked evidence for internal project reviews.
reach.learn: Evidence selection, source traceability and project review requirements.

evidence.claim: Indexed retrieval, access checks and controlled delivery are primarily configured records functions.
TOPdesk Robin answers from maintained knowledge and hands unresolved requests onward; this supports intake and handover, not archive access control.
The digest provides no measured file-retrieval case or guarantee of search accuracy.

assumptions: The target covers internal requests; external disclosure needs a separately defined release process.
Records owners participate in restricted or exceptional requests, rather than every routine retrieval.
Paper retrieval is a branch of the process; fully digital requests skip it.
Routine access follows existing permissions; exceptional access requires records-owner approval.
Copy checks retain time for physical scanning, version uncertainty and required exclusions.
Step shares include records-owner handling and are illustrative workflow effort, not a measured clerk-only time study.
These filing functions do not decide employment, credit or benefit outcomes; EU AI Act assessment follows the actual use.
Build estimates include access work and applicable consultation under national rules; archive cleanup is additional.

Whether search, previews and links enforce the same permissions.
How often retrieval requires redaction, external disclosure or original delivery.
Who owns restricted records and can approve access exceptions.
Whether current interfaces expose reliable versions and delivery events.

Handle denied access, redaction and disclosure exceptions.
Maintain taxonomy, indexing and records-owner assignments.
Test permission boundaries and failed or revoked delivery links.
Monitor extraction failures without retaining unnecessary confidential request text.
tasks.statement: Find, retrieve, and make copies of information from files in response to requests and deliver information to authorized users.

tasks.short: Support invoice processing, resolve discrepancies, accept cash payments and issue receipts.

steps.what: Receive supplier invoices and place them in the processing queue.
Read invoice details and enter a draft invoice record.

loop.output: Draft invoice fields and line items with source references.
loop.check: Check totals, currency, required fields, supplier match and duplicates; clerk confirms capture.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per invoice; unreadable or conflicting fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured invoices import directly; varying document layouts and free-text lines need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Compare invoice lines with purchase orders and goods receipts.
Discuss missing receipts, price differences and disputed charges with the responsible people.
Approve the charge against the departmental budget.
Post the approved invoice and pass it to finance for payment.
For cash payments, count tender and confirm the amount due.
Record the cash payment and issue its receipt.

tasks.design: Configured intake in the {WORKFLOW} imports structured invoices and uses bounded document extraction for other invoices before capture review. Matching and posting use the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}, with evidence packs for discrepancy conversations and budget-holder approval. A confirmed cash entry in the {ERP} creates the payment record and receipt; finance retains payment release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document variation, missing purchase evidence and approval handoffs prevented reliable straight-through processing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing matching and approval features can be configured, while bounded extraction reduces document rekeying. Faster connector development makes the remaining gaps cheaper to address.
tasks.still_hard: Non-purchase-order invoices, disputed delivery and supplier identity changes require investigation. Physical cash custody and payment authorisation remain separate responsibilities.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving commercial discrepancies and noticing when apparently valid paperwork describes a questionable charge.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of invoice discrepancies approaching payment deadlines.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from capture and matching toward discrepancy resolution and cash handling. Proposed delegation allows the clerk to return incomplete invoice packs and prioritise follow-up; spending approval and payment release remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of invoice mismatch and late approval.
reach.learn: Purchase-to-payment controls, exception categories and process measurement.

evidence.claim: Existing financial workflows can perform deterministic matching, approval routing, posting and receipt generation.
Rossum documents document capture, rule checking and exception routing for orders, supporting the extraction pattern.
The proposed invoice controls, time reductions and build ranges require local validation.

assumptions: This supporting role prepares payables; the finance team releases payments.
Invoice processing and cash collection are separate branches, not successive stages of one transaction.
The time split represents a mixed workload and includes other actors' handling time, excluding waiting.
Cash collection is a smaller branch; many employers will have none.
The {ERP} supports matching, approvals and receipt generation.
GDPR applies to personal financial data; model use requires assessment under the EU AI Act.
Consent and access estimates include financial permissions and applicable consultation under national rules.

Purchase-order coverage and availability of goods receipts.

Applicable consultation requirements and financial access lead times.

Handle unmatched invoices and failed postings.
Maintain matching tolerances and approval routing.
Reconcile payment records and generated receipts.
Review access and changes to financial workflow configuration.
tasks.statement: Complete general financial activities, such as processing accounts payable, reviewing invoices, collecting cash payments, or issuing receipts.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
